newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSIGHT - JGB futures seen maintaining weak tone.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - JGB futures seen maintaining weak tone.

text.p: Key June Japanese government bond (JGB) futures are expected to maintain a bearish tone on Monday's Tokyo trade, but may have a room for rebound after last week's sharp fall, traders said.
"The June could open lower in line with Friday's fall on LIFFE. However, it is unlikely to fall below last week's low of 122.70," said a trader at a city bank's securities unit.
The benchmark contract fell as low as 123.20 on Friday's LIFFE session, after closing at 123.45 in Tokyo.
Traders said a stronger yen and weak stocks may provide some support to JGBs.
The dollar fell below 118.00 yen in early Tokyo trade. It closed at 122.84/87 yen on Friday in Tokyo.
Traders said that if the Nikkei 225 stock average remained below the key 20,000 level, it would be positive for JGBs.
The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ) is expected to announce its long-term prime rate for May on Monday.
Traders expect the bank to raise its long-term prime rate by 0.6 or 0.7 percentage point.
"If IBJ debentures weaken further this morning, the long-term prime may be raised by 0.7 percent," said the trader at the city bank's securities unit.
IBJ's 1.6 percent five-year bank debenture issued in April was traded at 2.3 percent on Friday.
Traders said they will also be closely watching the reaction of U.S. Treasuries to U.S. inflation data to be released this week.
